clue.text: Priest volunteers to go in and float in air

indicators.note: the volunteers are told to enter the priest, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a Levite was a member of the Hebrew priestly tribe
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers to step inside and hover above the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volunteers' reads as a verb but is a noun: the TA, Britain's volunteer reserve army. 'to go in' places it inside the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to rise and hover unsupported, as a stage magician's assistant appears to.

clue.text: Ordinary people without the vote from carelessness

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the ordinary people stand around the vote

parts.note: the laity are those who are not clergy or experts
X is the cross a voter marks on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Disenfranchised commoners are the result of someone's negligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but here means 'outside': the people surround the X a voter marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: slackness or want of strictness in how something is done.

clue.text: National art collection originally looted by Germanic raider

parts.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London, Britain's national museum of art and design

indicators.note: originally asks for the opening letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A country's art treasures were first plundered by a barbarian invader.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A, London's Victoria and Albert Museum, is spelt out as V AND A; 'originally' takes the first letter of 'looted'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a member of the Germanic people who sacked Rome in 455.

clue.text: The rot broadcast about a strike, up to that time

indicators.note: the scattered letters go around the strike, enclosing it
seed that is broadcast is scattered, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: to strike something is to hit it

explanation.surface: Radio aired nonsense about an industrial stoppage until then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns THE ROT into THERTO, and 'about' wraps that round HIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an old-fashioned adverb meaning until then.

clue.text: Providing material for printers the sort encountered in Bridgend

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
something encountered has been found
taken as written
split as Bridg-end, the end of 'Bridg', which is its last letter G

explanation.surface: Supplying print shops with the kind of thing you come across in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridgend is a town in South Wales, but here it must be split: the end of 'Bridg' is G. 'sort' is itself a printer's word for a piece of type, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: the trade of casting the metal letters that printers set.

clue.text: Good, trusty people — but what cards!

definitions.meaning: British informal praise for reliable, generous folk, as in 'you're a real brick'
those of the suit that outranks the other three in whist or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: informally, dependable generous people, and the playing cards of the suit that beats all others.

clue.text: Respond with about-turn

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in a memo heading
a turn is an act in a variety show

explanation.surface: Answer by spinning round to face the other way.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'about-turn' must be split into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to act in answer to something.

clue.text: Bloomer made by a fellow navigator

parts.note: a fellow is a man
Sir Francis Drake, the Elizabethan sailor who circumnavigated the globe

explanation.surface: A mistake committed by a colleague reading the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' is British slang for a blunder, but here it is something that blooms: a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a plant, since it blooms, this one famous for its forked root.

clue.text: Hat exhibited in county circle, worn by Harris's brother

indicators.note: the county and circle are worn by the brother, so he fills them as a wearer fills a garment

parts.note: Som is the abbreviation for Somerset, a county in south-west England
the letter O is a circle in shape
Brer is how Joel Chandler Harris wrote 'brother' in his Uncle Remus tales, as in Brer Rabbit

explanation.surface: Headgear on display at a local society event, sported by a man's sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: Harris is Joel Chandler Harris, the American author of the Uncle Remus tales, where 'brother' is a title given to Rabbit and Fox. 'worn by' is the container signal; the surface suggests a county show.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the broad-brimmed Mexican kind.

clue.text: Shrewish woman cross with worker repairing pipe

parts.note: the letter X is a cross in shape
a worker ant is the crossword's usual labourer

indicators.note: repairing something means reworking it, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered wife is angry with the plumber fixing a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is not her mood but the letter X; 'repairing' turns PIPE into IPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of Socrates' wife, proverbial for a nagging, bad-tempered spouse.

clue.text: Publication by miners shows lots of bottle!

parts.note: mag is short for magazine
the NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British coal miners' trade union

explanation.surface: A pitmen's newsletter displays plenty of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' is British slang for nerve, but here it is literal: a large amount of bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful description: a wine bottle holding twice the normal amount.

clue.text: Clay from a worthy chronicler's underground home?

parts.note: Thomas Fuller wrote The Worthies of England (1662); the possessive gives his name with an S
an earth is a fox's burrow

explanation.surface: Soil taken from the burrow of a respectable historian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worthy' hints at Thomas Fuller's Worthies of England, so the chronicler of worthies is Fuller. An earth is where a fox lives.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind: an absorbent clay once used for cleaning wool.

clue.text: Show staged in Harrogate — A Chorus Line

indicators.note: what is staged in a venue appears inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

explanation.surface: A Broadway musical is being put on in a Yorkshire spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a noun for the musical but is a verb. 'staged in' finds the letters running across the end of Harrogate, A, and the start of Chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to show someone how to do something is to instruct them.

clue.text: Mandarins may bring him part of his income

definitions.text: Mandarins may bring him part of his income

parts.words: Mandarins may bring him part of his income
parts.note: mandarins are not high officials here but small oranges, which a certain shopkeeper sells for a living

explanation.definitionFit: A description: a shopkeeper who earns money selling oranges and similar produce.

clue.text: Agitator beginning to torment Russian wage-earner

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: whimsically, someone who makes roubles, the Russian currency, as a wage-earner makes money

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser starts to harass a worker in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Russian wage-earner is a whimsical 'rouble maker', one who makes roubles; 'beginning to' adds the first letter of 'torment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone who stirs up unrest.

clue.text: Came to road works, having left behind a line of cars

indicators.note: the letters are worked, that is manipulated into a new order
the fodder has left a letter behind, so the letter named next is dropped from it

parts.note: the letter to drop, as written

explanation.surface: Arriving at a stretch of roadworks after overtaking a queue of traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left behind a' drops one A from CAME TO ROAD, and 'works' rearranges the remaining nine letters. The 'a' belongs to the wordplay, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a procession of vehicles, such as one escorting a president.

clue.text: Very clean, though without special lighting

definitions.meaning: immaculate, with no mark of dirt anywhere
whimsically, lacking spots, the theatre's short name for spotlights

explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate in the ordinary sense; and read whimsically, lacking the spotlights a theatre uses.

clue.text: Warning device that works on rollers

definitions.text: Warning device that works on rollers

parts.words: Warning device that works on rollers
parts.note: the rollers are not wheels or cylinders but sea waves, whose motion makes this floating marker ring

explanation.definitionFit: A description: a floating marker that rings as the waves rock it, alerting ships to danger.

clue.text: Ordered red notepaper, to carry more weight

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone bought scarlet stationery so their letters would have more impact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like a purchase but means arranged: the letters of RED NOTEPAPER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to outweigh, or be greater in influence or number.

clue.text: Girl seen around northern yacht station

indicators.note: the girl is seen around the next piece, so her name encloses it

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman spotted near a boat club up north.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a harbour with moorings for pleasure boats.

clue.text: Absence of design for uncompleted part of church

indicators.note: an uncompleted thing lacks its finish, so the word described loses its last letter

parts.note: the chancel is the area of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: No plans exist for the unfinished section of the cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' is not an architect's drawing but intention. 'uncompleted' drops the final L from CHANCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: what happens by accident, with no intention behind it.

clue.text: Capacity to endure permitted variation

definitions.meaning: the ability to bear something, such as pain or a drug
in engineering, the allowed margin by which a part's size may differ from the specification

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the ability to bear something, and an engineer's allowable margin of error in a measurement.

clue.text: Arrested knight overwhelmed by downfall

indicators.note: the knight is swamped by the downfall, so it is engulfed inside that word

parts.note: someone's downfall is their ruin
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A captured nobleman is crushed by his fall from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overwhelmed by' puts the chess knight's N inside RUIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A slang synonym as a past participle: a suspect who has been taken into custody.

clue.text: Fish in river, at first opposite a church

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the neighbouring word

explanation.surface: Angling in a stream that initially faced a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a common freshwater species of the carp family.

clue.text: Like Bucephalus, one of five in similar quarters

indicators.note: the one of five is placed inside the pair of quarters

parts.note: quarters are compass points, and two the same are E and E, east twice
a quin is one of quintuplets, five children born together

explanation.surface: Resembling Alexander's steed, one of a handful stabled in matching lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucephalus was Alexander the Great's horse. 'in' puts QUIN, a quintuplet, between two identical compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective meaning horse-like, and Alexander the Great's famous mount was a horse.

clue.text: Gold vessel captivates a girl from the islands

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: to captivate is to hold captive, so the vessel holds the next pieces inside it

parts.note: a can is a container for liquid
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: A golden ship enchants a young woman who comes from an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' is a can, not a ship; 'captivates' has it hold A and DI. The islands are Orkney, off the north coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something or someone belonging to Orkney, the Scottish island group.

clue.text: Saw, for example, gin circulating

parts.note: say is used to mean for example

indicators.note: what circulates moves around, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: Noticed, for instance, the spirits being passed round the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the past of 'see' but a noun, an old proverb; 'circulating' turns GIN into ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a saw is a proverb or maxim.

clue.text: Holes made by expert for this fastener

indicators.note: the letters are made, that is fashioned, into a new arrangement

parts.note: an ace is an expert, as in a flying ace

explanation.surface: A craftsman has punched openings so that this fastening can go through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges HOLES into SHOEL. The surface describes the answer too, since it threads through holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a cord threaded through eyelets to tie footwear closed.
